# Self-serve: Gupshup API MCP

For developers and businesses on the **Gupshup messaging API** ([reference](https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/msg)). This MCP server is hosted on the Gupshup docs portal. Connect it to your AI client and your agent can work with the messaging API: WhatsApp, SMS, RCS and more.

> Enterprise customers (analytics, templates and campaigns through OAuth sign-in) use the [Enterprise server](clients/README.md) instead. You can connect both.

| | |
|---|---|
| Server URL | `https://docs.gupshup.io/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Auth | Your Gupshup **API key** in the `apikey` header |
| API reference | https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/msg |

**Get your API key** from your Gupshup account dashboard. Keep it out of shared or committed files: the snippets below read it from the `GUPSHUP_API_KEY` environment variable, or prompt for it.

```bash
export GUPSHUP_API_KEY="<your Gupshup API key>"
```

## Claude Code
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gupshup-api https://docs.gupshup.io/mcp --header "apikey: $GUPSHUP_API_KEY"
```

## Cursor
[![Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/deeplink/mcp-install-dark.svg)](https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=gupshup-api&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2RvY3MuZ3Vwc2h1cC5pby9tY3AiLCJoZWFkZXJzIjp7ImFwaWtleSI6IiR7ZW52OkdVUFNIVVBfQVBJX0tFWX0ifX0%3D)

The button adds the server with the key read from `GUPSHUP_API_KEY`: set that variable, then restart Cursor. Or add it to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` yourself:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gupshup-api": {
      "url": "https://docs.gupshup.io/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "apikey": "${env:GUPSHUP_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## VS Code
`.vscode/mcp.json`. VS Code prompts for the key once and stores it securely:
```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "gupshup-api-key",
      "description": "Gupshup API key",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "gupshup-api": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://docs.gupshup.io/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "apikey": "${input:gupshup-api-key}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## OpenAI Codex CLI
`~/.codex/config.toml`:
```toml
[mcp_servers.gupshup-api]
url = "https://docs.gupshup.io/mcp"
env_http_headers = { "apikey" = "GUPSHUP_API_KEY" }
```

## Windsurf / Devin Desktop
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gupshup-api": {
      "serverUrl": "https://docs.gupshup.io/mcp",
      "headers": {

      }
    }
  }

```

## Claude Desktop and other stdio-only clients
Use the [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote) bridge to add the header:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gupshup-api": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "https://docs.gupshup.io/mcp",
        "--header",
        "apikey:${GUPSHUP_API_KEY}"
      ],
      "env": {
        "GUPSHUP_API_KEY": "<your Gupshup API key>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Claude.ai and ChatGPT (web)
Their custom connectors authenticate with OAuth and don't let you set an API-key header, so this server can't be added there yet. Use one of the clients above.

## Security
- Your API key can send messages and incur charges, so treat it like a password. Don't paste it into chats, issues or committed config files.
- Rotate the key from your Gupshup dashboard if it's exposed.
- Keep your client's tool-approval prompts on for anything that sends messages.

No account yet? Sign up at [gupshup.ai](https://www.gupshup.ai), or talk to [sales](mailto:sales@gupshup.ai).
